name: Swingo Poker
description: Poker variant in which players bet on the best five-card hand, using their own five cards (three exposed), one shared face-up river card, and one exposed card from any other player.

overview.description: Poker variant in which players bet on the best five-card hand, using their own five cards (three exposed), one shared face-up river card, and one exposed card from any other player.

history.origins: Invented by Steve Albini in December 2007 and developed by the Alliance-X poker group in Chicago. Named after a classic Chicago punk song by Naked Raygun.
timeline: 2007 onward: Alliance-X poker group in Chicago refines rules.
history.cultural: Reflects Chicago home-game poker culture and punk music reference.
history.evolution: Combines stud-like exposed boards with one shared river card and the unique rule that each player may use one exposed card from another player's board.

setup.players: Two to eight players; best with five to eight.
setup.dealing: Before the deal, the player to dealer's left posts the small blind and the next player posts the big blind (twice the small blind). Dealer shuffles and cuts, then deals five cards face down to each player.
setup.equipment: Standard deck and poker chips. Stakes (blinds and pot limit) agreed before play.

rules.objective: Win the pot by making the best five-card poker hand from seven cards: your two hole cards, your three board cards, the shared river card, and any one exposed card from another player's board.
rules.gameplay: After the deal and first betting round, each player chooses two hole cards (hidden) and three board cards (exposed). All expose their boards; second betting round, started by the highest board. Dealer deals one shared river card to the center; third betting round, again started by highest board. Showdown: each player makes the best five-card hand from their two hole cards, three board cards, river card, and one card from any other player's board. Best hand wins; ties split the pot.
keyRules: Blinds (small and big) are posted before the deal by the two players to dealer's left.
First betting round is started by the player left of the big blind.
Each player must choose two hole cards and three board cards; boards are exposed simultaneously.
Second and third betting rounds are started by the surviving player with the highest ranking set of board cards (pairs, two pair, trips count; incomplete straights and flushes do not).
A player may only fold when facing a bet or raise they are unwilling to call; if already matching the current bet they cannot fold (others may need their board card).
At showdown each player may use any five of their seven available cards; the river and another player's board card are optional.
Board cards of folded players are mucked face down; surviving players' board cards remain visible for others to use.

strategy.basic: Track which board cards opponents have; they may need one of yours at showdown.
strategy.intermediate: Bet in the third round to force folds and remove a card another player might need for their hand.
strategy.advanced: If you can see a player has a strong hand (e.g. straight flush visible), bet to make others fold so their key board card is mucked and that hand is no longer possible.
tips: Folding removes your board cards from the table; sometimes calling keeps a card in play that hurts the leader.
Board order for first to act: pairs, two pair, and trips count; incomplete straights and flushes do not.

variations.name: Sweet Chariot
variations.description: Lowball variant: played like Swingo but the lowest hand wins the pot at showdown.

variations.name: High-Low with declaration
variations.description: Played with limit betting and a chips-in-fist declaration of high, low, or both before showdown; pot split per declarations.

scoring.description: Standard poker hand rankings. Each player makes the best five-card hand from seven cards (two hole, three board, river, one from another's board). Best hand wins the pot; ties split equally.
scoring.winCondition: Best five-card poker hand from the seven available cards (two hole, three board, river, one from another player's board) wins the pot. Ties split the pot.
